items.title: Verstappen takes the season's first pole; Hamilton alongside on a 0.298s margin
items.summary: Verstappen set 1:35.130 in Q3, 0.298s clear of Hamilton, with Hadjar third, Antonelli fourth and Leclerc fifth on the raw classification. Official results show Verstappen fastest in Q1 and Q2 as well. The Race notes the Verstappen-Hamilton front row echoes the 2017 Malaysian race.
items.why_it_matters: It is Verstappen's first pole of 2026 and the first Sepang race in nine years. Formula1.com's strategy guide says track position may count for less on Sunday than the grid suggests; treat that as reporting, not a forecast.

sources.label: The Race: starting grid after three penalties

items.title: Three power-unit penalties reshape the grid behind the front row
items.summary: FIA decisions list Hadjar (car 6) with a five-place drop, Colapinto (car 43) with ten and Lindblad (car 41) with thirty. Hadjar qualified third on pace, so the sanction applies to his grid slot; Formula1.com says Russell's eighth-place qualifying result becomes a seventh-place start.
items.why_it_matters: Use the official post-qualifying grid for starting positions. The ten-place figure for Colapinto is what the FIA document states; earlier reports cited five from his Baku carry-over, so quote the decision document.

items.title: Upgraded Mercedes lose pace in Qualifying: Russell perplexed, Antonelli rues an error
items.summary: Russell was eighth after Mercedes brought a seven-item package declared in FIA Document 12; he said he could not explain the lost Qualifying pace and expects a different story in the race. Antonelli qualified fourth and said a front-row start was possible.
items.why_it_matters: Mercedes had been quick in FP3 (Antonelli fastest) before this Qualifying drop, so race-pace evidence matters more than the grid. The cause has not been established by the sources reviewed.

items.title: Norris says McLaren are 'a long way off the pace' on their first Sepang visit
items.summary: Norris qualified sixth and Piastri seventh, 0.627s and 0.632s behind pole. Norris said McLaren are struggling; neither driver had raced at Sepang before.
items.why_it_matters: A reigning champion publicly describing a large deficit is a race-day storyline; verify against long-run pace once the race starts.

sources.label: Formula1.com: What the teams said, Qualifying

items.title: Aston Martin reach Q2 on merit and start 12th and 14th; Hadjar returns with a strong car
items.summary: Alonso (12th) and Stroll (14th) both advanced to Q2 on merit after a poor run in Monza, Baku and Madrid. Hadjar, in only his second race back from a wrist injury, qualified third before his penalty.
items.why_it_matters: These are the grid-position and recovery stories most likely to feature early in the race under the official Heat Hazard declaration.
